scope: Every claim Paper II (paper/research2/manuscript.tex) makes or will make about Research 2 as a whole, cross-referenced to repository evidence. Complements, and does not replace, paper/research2/claims/claim_ledger.md (II-A/II-B scoped) which this ledger extends in spirit for II-C.

claims.text: decayed_transition (decay=0.99) improves held-out causal prediction quality over both trivial causal baselines at the primary horizon (h=1): EVAL mean recall 0.449817 vs last_observation 0.401473 (+12.04% relative) and vs global_frequency 0.349480 (+28.71% relative).
claims.scope: Prediction quality only; DEV-anchored Category B classification SUPPORTED not promoted by EVAL

claims.text: Predictive information about future expert routing contains exploitable structure beyond trivial frequency/recency baselines (synthesis of R2-05/06/07 descriptive structure + R2-09/10 predictor margin).
claims.scope: Structure and exploitability of a measurable margin; not a proof of maximal exploitability.

claims.text: Replay-level retention (miss_bytes_per_decode_step) improves under the predictor-driven PredictedProtect policy relative to B_selected(M) at the primary 4 GiB budget: mean delta -87,476.85 bytes/decode-step, 95% CI [-154123.32, -27178.93] entirely below zero. Classification R2_11_PASS.
claims.statistical_support: R2-BRIDGE-01: 4 held-out instances, all workloads <=0. R2-11: 72/72 cells, paired bootstrap 95% CI, 100000 resamples.
claims.scope: Replay-level metric only (miss_bytes_per_decode_step); NOT a runtime/latency/throughput measurement.

claims.text: The tested real-runtime PredictedProtect realization does NOT improve real-runtime decode throughput (tokens/second) over B_selected(M) at the frozen primary 4 GiB budget: observed mean delta_tps = -0.171721, 95% CI [-0.259917, -0.091642], entirely <=0.
claims.statistical_support: 40 counted launches (20/policy), paired bootstrap 95% CI per frozen statistical_analysis.json
claims.scope: Real-runtime decode throughput at the primary 4 GiB budget, this host/runtime/model configuration only.

claims.text: The primary R2-12 result is negative: classification R2_12_FAIL, based strictly on the frozen 4 GiB primary endpoint.
claims.scope: Primary classification only; secondary 1.5/8 GiB budgets do not override it.

claims.text: Predictive retention universally fails (as a general proposition beyond the tested realization/host/model/workloads).
claims.reason_not_supported: Only one reactive predictive-retention realization was tested, on one host/model/workload family. R2-11's replay-level result was positive; only the specific real-runtime conversion failed.

R2-10 demonstrated a measurable, held-out-confirmed prediction-quality margin over trivial baselines (C-SUP-1). R2-12's negative runtime result does not invalidate this, as prediction quality and real-runtime throughput are different, separately-scoped measurements.

claims.text: The R2-11 replay-level retention benefit was invalid or an artifact.
claims.reason_not_supported: R2-11 used a frozen, preregistered protocol, a paired bootstrap with 100,000 resamples, and a 95% CI entirely below zero across 72/72 cells with 0 failures. It is not invalidated by R2-12's unrelated real-runtime measurement.

claims.text: Policy/non-retention overhead is proven to cause the R2-12 runtime loss.
claims.reason_not_supported: The real 8 GiB null-control canonical records contain no retention-traffic telemetry for either policy (expert_bytes_read/expert_read_count/expert_miss_bytes and expert_io_best_effort sub-fields are all None). Any overhead attribution therefore remains an unverified hypothesis.

claims.text: The 8 GiB real-runtime loss proves a monotonic memory-budget effect on policy overhead.
claims.reason_not_supported: Only three budget points were tested (1.5/4/8 GiB); ordered magnitudes (smallest at 1.5 GiB, largest at 8 GiB) are an observation, not a proof of monotonic causal dependence.

claims.text: Increasing memory budget necessarily increases predictive-policy overhead in general.
claims.reason_not_supported: No causal mechanism was isolated; the observed ordering at three tested points is descriptive only.

claims.text: R2-12 proves that predictive prefetch (as opposed to the tested reactive retention realization) would fail.
claims.reason_not_supported: R2-12 tested one reactive retention policy realization, not a prefetch/overlap/scheduling design. These are explicitly out of scope and left as future-work directions, not refuted findings.

claims.text: R2-12 proves that no predictive runtime optimization can succeed in this problem class.
claims.reason_not_supported: A single negative result for one tested realization on one host/model/workload configuration does not establish impossibility for the broader design space.

claims.text: R2-11 was NOT PROPOSED under the original frozen R2-10 decision rules.
claims.note: Remains true and unchanged under the R2-10 decision rules' own DEV-anchored text. R2-BRIDGE-01's prospective evidence, generated under a new, separate, later-frozen contract, subsequently justified proposing R2-11 as its own protocol. This does not rewrite the historical statement; both are true simultaneously.
